meta.title: Third sweep, batch 03: New searches and page reads: money, grants and organisations
meta.status: collection only; nothing in this file is on the map or in data/
meta.access_note: Pages were read with a page-reader tool, because the working container cannot reach these hosts directly. Most reads returned the page text; some returned the reader's own extract of the page instead (claims from those carry access = page_read_via_reader_extract). Each claim's evidence_text was checked by script against what the reader returned for that URL.
meta.stopped_agents_note: Some searches and reads in this batch were stopped by the account usage limit before they reported. Their searches and page-reader calls are logged in raw/ as returned, but produced no claims. Agents that were run again after the limit reset are listed in stats.agents_rerun_after_usage_limit; any still missing are in stats.agents_stopped_at_usage_limit.

evidence_check_values.normalized: found after normalising spaces, quote marks and dashes
evidence_check_values.normalized_ci: found after normalising and ignoring case
evidence_check_values.segments: excerpt contains an ellipsis; every part was found
evidence_check_values.not_found: not found in the captured page text: treat the claim as unverified
evidence_check_values.no_raw: no page text was captured for this URL
evidence_check_values.*_in_reader_extract: the page reader returned an extract rather than the page text; the excerpt was found in that extract (a page-text re-check is pending)
evidence_check_values.found_on_linked_page: not on the page at url, but found word for word on another page the same reader opened from it (see evidence_found_at)
evidence_check_values.found_in_reader_extract_only: the page text was captured later and the excerpt is not in it word for word; it is only in the page reader's own extract, so treat the wording as unverified

meta.labels: fact | alleged | speculation | unproven_conspiracy | no_link. fact = the source states it (or the organisation published it about itself). label_scope says what the label covers.

map_status_values.pair_already_linked: both entities are on the map and already linked (see existing_relations)
map_status_values.new_tie_between_known_entities: both entities are on the map but not linked
map_status_values.new_entity_or_unmatched_name: one side matched a map entity, the other did not (new entity, or a name the matcher missed)
map_status_values.both_names_unmatched: neither side matched a map entity

meta.translations: evidence_translation is a literal English translation written for this file, not the source's own wording.

pages.capture_answer: Ministry of Justice news item dated 12.06.2024. The ceremony took place at the Ministry of Justice. Minister of Justice Adam Bodnar gave Iver Ørstavik the Badge of Honor for Merits to the Administration of Justice (body text also calls it the Badge of Honor for Merits in the Field of Justice). Stated reasons: contributions to strengthening democratic-state principles, legal culture and the justice system. Bodnar cited Ørstavik's work on Norwegian-Polish NGO collaboration for the rule of law. Attendees: Deputy Minister of Justice Zuzanna Rudzińska-Bluszcz, Norwegian Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Marta Varteressian, Norwegian Ambassador to Poland Øystein Bø, and unnamed Polish NGO and academic representatives. Ørstavik is called an activist with the Rafto Foundation for Human Rights, not a Rafto adviser. The page does not mention a Norway Grants freeze, Ziobro, support for Polish judges, or any amount. No funders, organiser details or party affiliations are stated.

pages.capture_answer: The landing page has only the title and a link to the PDF. The PDF is the exhibit set (Exhibits 1 to 5, 21 pages) from Case 1:12-cv-02034-RBW, Document 31-1, filed 09/16/15. Its docket notices come from Judicial Watch, Inc. v. Department of State, No. 1:13-cv-01363-EGS (D.D.C.), a FOIA suit about former Secretary Clinton's private email server and State Department records. The exhibits are minute orders dated July 31, August 7 and August 20, 2015; a September 2, 2015 letter from the State Department to the FBI General Counsel; State Department letters to the FBI Director and to Clinton's attorney; a June 15, 2015 reply from that attorney; and a NARA letter dated July 2, 2016 (OCR 'JUL. 0 2 2016'). The FOIA request they describe seeks Huma Abedin's SF-50 personnel forms, State Department contracts with her, and records of her outside employment. No released record names Free Courts, Batory, HFHR, Iustitia, Themis or DemoCrisis, or shows State or embassy money to any of them. No amounts appear. The exhibits do not mention Poland, a US embassy, or the Open Society Foundations. Officials' names are in names_listed.

pages.capture_answer: The programme 'Strengthening Democratic Resilience and Civil Society in Poland' is listed for Action For Democracy. The country 'United States' is inferred, not written. Programme amount: 'Not stated' on the listing; the profile shows 'Amount Varies'. The $318K figure is the funder's total 2024 grants (one grant, $317,960 in the profile table, to Khmer Democratic Rescue Foundation, Pomona, CA), not this programme's budget. Dates: rolling (quarterly review); 'Tracked since April 2026'; the listing also gives a first-round deadline of 'July 17, 6pm CET (2023)'. Eligibility: non-governmental, non-partisan CSOs based in Poland, with national reach or rural operation valued, and compliant with all Polish and U.S. rules, including electoral and campaign finance laws. Named grantees for Poland: none. Places where the profile says the funder has awarded grants: California, District of Columbia, New York, Virginia. Iustitia, Themis, Free Courts / Wolne Sądy, HFHR, Batory Foundation, KOS, OKO.press, Akcja Demokracja and KOD are not named. Funder board (2024 filing, per profile): David Koranyi (Board President; compensation $298K in 2024), Christopher Maroshegyi (Board Treasurer; $27K), Elisabeth Jennings (Board Secretary), Roberto Patino (Board Member). The funder's own grantee list was not checked: its website is linked from the profile but sits on another host. The 2022 and 2023 grantee names did not come through in the fetched text. pages.page_title: Zapytanie w sprawie Prokuratury Krajowej
pages.capture_answer: Written question no. 289 was submitted by Ewa Leniart and Fryderyk Sylwester Kapinos, received 06-02-2024, to the Minister of Justice about the Prokuratura Krajowa. It names three opinion authors, dr hab. Sławomirowi Patyrze, dr Hannie Rakowskiej and dr hab. Grzegorzowi Kule, for opinions on restoring prosecutor Dariusz Barski to active service, and asks when and on what terms they were commissioned, including the 'wysokość wynagrodzenia' (amount of remuneration). The page gives no fee amount, contract number or payment date. Question 2 asks whether any expert had earlier worked with Adam Bodnar as an NGO activist or during his RPO tenure; questions 3 and 5 concern agreements between Bodnar and Donald Tusk and the appointment of Jacek Bilewicz. The page has no Ministry reply, so the requested MoJ answer attachment with amounts and payment dates is not captured. Of the listed judges, Tusk, Bodnar and NGOs, only Patyra (as expert), Bodnar and Tusk appear, and no NGO is named.

pages.capture_answer: Protocol of the PROO Priorytet 4 Edycja 2025 expert panel, Warsaw, 12 marca 2025 r.; NIW-CRSO supervised it. The page says 97 experts took part in the assessment and that 20 were drawn by lottery on 19 lutego 2025 r., with 10 reserves. names_listed holds the 20 drawn experts; 18 of them appear in the attendance and signature lists, while Paweł Tokarczyk and Wioletta Gawrońska appear only in the draw table. The reserves are Wojciech Ziętara, Agnieszka Grzesiak, Bartosz Kordala, Anna Janczyk-Zabrocka, Jakub Drożdż, Ewelina Wojciechowska, Arkadiusz Banaś, Piotr Nowacki, Danuta Bień and Damian Ziółek. Three NIW-CRSO staff attended without a vote: Adela Gąsiorowska, Stefan Kołucki and Katarzyna Asińska-Paluch. Four applications were voted on: 70376 Fundacja Instrat (score 189), 74453 Fundacja imienia Braci Sołuńskich - Cyryla i Metodego, 75290 Fundacja Instytut Polityk Publicznych (score 189) and 76158 Fundacja PRO POSNANIA. The page does not say which applications were funded or how much any applicant received. It says 20 applications were recommended down to the 189-point threshold but does not name them; the protocol says the ranked lists were presented with proposed grant amounts, but those lists are not in the page text. No expert fees are stated. Kultura Liberalna, application 77143, Watchdog Polska, ISP, INPRIS, CEO, HFHR and Akcja Demokracja do not appear. A scan of the page text found none of the eight judges, nor Iustitia, Themis, Wolne Sądy, Batory, KOS, OKO.press, Akcja Demokracja or KOD. Declared conflicts of interest: Dorota Głażewska-Ziemilska (74684, 70622) and Katarzyna Lipka-Szostak (73599); the applicants behind these numbers are not named.

The article is dated 18 grudnia 2017 and its finance figures are for 2017, not 2026. The sidebar shows 2026 headlines, but the article body is from 2017. A top banner ('Dzisiaj Dzień Bez Oka...') is undated. The endorser sentence is cut off after 'Iwona' in the fetched text. Page metadata shows modified 2026-11-02.
pages.page_title: Kto stoi za OKO.press? Szczera do bólu informacja o naszych finansach
pages.capture_answer: Year: the article is dated 18 grudnia 2017 and its figures are for 2017, not 2026. Income: average monthly income in 2017 was 104, 8 tys. zł (page spacing), of which reader payments 92 tys. a month (average January to November 2017) and grants 12,8 tys. a month. Shares computed from these figures (not stated on the page): readers about 88%, grants about 12%. The article gives no 1.5% share. The follow-up 1.5% page gives a statement that 1.5% equals 24% of the annual budget, and one-off reader payments averaging 50 000 zł a month; neither has a year. Named grant-makers with amounts (2017): Fundacji Batorego 40 tys. zł and the British Sigrid Rausing Trust 113 360 zł. The page says the Batory grant ends 'Od stycznia' and the Sigrid Rausing Trust grant 'od maja 2018'. Start-up money (2016, no amounts) came from Polityka Sp. z o.o. S.K.A., Agora Holding Sp. z o.o. and one unnamed private person. Other figures stated: monthly budget 132,5 tys. zł; monthly shortfall 27,7 tys.; 7613 people who have paid at least once, 2010 regularly; 2017 income did not cover costs. Arithmetic, not on the page: 40 000 + 113 360 = 153 360 zł, close to 12 x 12,8 thousand = 153 600 zł, which may mean the two grant figures are annual totals; the page does not say so. The seven names in names_listed are people the page says urge readers to support OKO.press; the sentence is cut off after 'Iwona'.

followup_urls.why: 'O nas' page linked in the footer; not fetched or checked for financial statements.
Archiwum Osiatyńskiego site linked from the page; the article says the Archive will publish its own reports. Not fetched.

pages.page_title: Wszystkie pieniądze KOD-u. Ile zebrali, na co wydali?
pages.capture_answer: Article dated 5 Jan 2017 (not 2026). TVN24 estimates that up to 2.5 mln zł may have reached KOD in 2016. Income as stated: public box collections 'prawie 1,1 mln złotych' (data for 5.12.2015-30.09.2016); membership fees about 1.08 mln (TVN24 arithmetic: about 9,000 members x 120 zł); private donations about 505 tys. zł (estimate). Spending: board declaration that funds went, among other things, to organising demonstrations. Payments: about 90 tys. zł to Kijowski's company MKM Studio, six invoices of about 15 tys. zł each, services March-August 2016. Named KOD people: Mateusz Kijowski (led KOD; company president), Radomir Szumełda (KOD board), Andrzej Blikle (financial-transparency adviser). No treasurer or finance officer, named donor, or foreign money is named. No further links on the page point to documents.

Headline 2025 figures: total revenue 47 972 644,98 zł, state subsidy (subwencja) 23 875 901,46 zł, bank loans 15 000 000,00 zł; Election Fund expenses 14 058 654,28 zł, of which 13 966 365,96 zł was allocated to presidential elections. No payee or vendor is named for any line. The full report and its attached auditor's report are referenced but not in the text, and no link to them appears. Items A-D seek State Department contracts and grant agreements with Free Courts ('Wolne Sady'), Civil Liberties Union for Europe, DemoCrisis and Ökotárs Alapítvány (Hungary). Item E seeks all State emails and cables mentioning these four groups. The complaint says no determination was made and no records were produced. It names no grant or amount and does not mention NED, OSF, Batory, HFHR, Iustitia or OKO.press. It references no exhibits.

pages.capture_answer: The MoJ register for 2024 (visible rows January to mid-June 2024, Bodnar's term as minister) lists paid opinion contracts. Patyra: PLN 3,000 (5 Jan, prosecution law). Rakowska's law office: PLN 3,001.20 and Kuca: PLN 3,000 (5 Jan, art. 47 of the 2016 introductory act to the Prosecution Law). Zalasiński, Urbaniak and Zaleśny: PLN 4,000 each (17-24 Jan, scope of TK interim measures). Kmieciak: two rows of PLN 3,723 (26 Feb, effects of the TK interim orders of 1 Feb 2024). Piotrowski: PLN 4,000 (4 Mar, effects of TK interim orders). Future TK judge Dziurda: PLN 8,000 (2-22 Apr, analysis of the draft law transposing the EU representative-actions directive). Other rows cover seconding judges to the MoJ, cancelling judicial competitions, presidential consent to deputy prosecutor appointments, lay judges (Gwizdak, PLN 20,333.23) and an audit firm's Justice Fund analysis (PLN 142,950.60). The visible rows contain no contract with the other six Sejm-elected TK judges, nor with Batory, HFHR, Iustitia, Themis or Free Courts.

pages.page_title: Umowy zawarte w 2024 roku
pages.capture_answer: In January-March 2024 the MoJ paid small fees (PLN 3,000-8,000) for legal opinions on the TK interim orders and on the National Prosecutor dispute. The TK-order opinions came from Zalasiński, Urbaniak, Zaleśny, Kmieciak and R. Piotrowski. The National Prosecutor opinions came from Patyra, Rakowska's law office and Kuca. Patyra and Dziurda became TK judges in 2026; Patyra was paid PLN 3,000 and Dziurda PLN 8,000 for an April 2024 analysis on a different subject. The MoJ also paid DemoCrisis PLN 31,500 to co-organise its April 2024 summit. The communications office (BK) bought media monitoring, social-media content and event services. No rule-of-law or TK information campaign appears in the visible rows.

pages.page_title: MoJ collective reply to written questions 3150-3182, 3188-3200, 3217-3220 and 3222-3238 (file z03182-o1)
pages.capture_answer: A single reply dated 3 Apr 2026, signed by Secretary of State Arkadiusz Myrcha and addressed to Marshal Czarzasty. It answers MP Dariusz Matecki's 67 written questions on 86 MoJ civil-law contracts of 2024, including no. 3200 on the Hoffman Taborowski contract. The reply points to the published 2024 contract register, argues the questions do not meet the requirements for parliamentary questions, and asks the Marshal to accept one collective answer. It names no contractor, contract number or amount, and does not mention Taborowski, Hoffman, the TK, the KRS or any judge.
